blocks.etymology: Borrowed from Portuguese inhame and Spanish ñame, likely from Wolof ñàmbi (“cassava”) or a related word. The term was spelled yam as early as 1657.

senses.definition: A large, long root of a tropical climbing plant, eaten cooked as a vegetable.

examples.en: Boiled yams are a staple food in many African countries.
examples.vi: Khoai mỡ luộc là lương thực chính ở nhiều quốc gia châu Phi.

senses.definition: A sweet potato, especially one with orange flesh that is baked or roasted.

examples.en: We baked sweet yams with butter for Thanksgiving dinner.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi đã nướng khoai lang với bơ cho bữa tối Lễ Tạ Ơn.

thesaurus.definition: edible tuber of any of several yams
any of a number of tropical vines of the genus Dioscorea many having edible tuberous roots
sweet potato with deep orange flesh that remains moist when baked
edible tuberous root of various yam plants of the genus Dioscorea grown in the tropics world-wide for food

wiktionary.gloss: Any climbing vine of the genus Dioscorea in the Eastern and Western hemispheres, usually cultivated.
The edible, starchy, tuberous root of that plant, a tropical staple food.
A sweet potato; a tuber from the species Ipomoea batatas.
A potato.
An oca; a tuber from the species Oxalis tuberosa.
Taro.
An orange-brown colour, like the flesh of the yam.
Home.

blocks.etymology: Ultimately from Fula nyaamude (“to eat”) or a cognate Fula-Wolof term.

wiktionary.gloss: To eat.

examples: For quotations using this term, see Citations:yam.
wiktionary.gloss: To dunk on; to beat humiliatingly.
